column1: # Tier 2 tolerances: backend<TAB>dtype<TAB>family-or-artifact<TAB>median<TAB>p90. Last match wins; * = any.
# Gated on the median and 90th percentile of the per-output errors (tier2.py compare): each
# output's error is rms(device − golden) over its reference rms, floored. Train steps compare
# out − in. Uncorrelated garbage scores ~1.4 on both.
# Set 2026-10-02 at ~3× what CUDA (4060 Ti, TF32 on) measured against XLA:CPU. The deep
# batch-BN nets at random init are chaotic in bf16: XLA:CPU against ITSELF, inputs scaled by
# 1 + 1e-6, already spreads p90 0.66 (MobileNetV2) / 0.59 (ResNet-34). Their p90 is
# therefore not gated (3), only the median. A new backend starts from these rows.
# Checked by breaking artifacts on purpose (one conv kernel's spatial dims swapped, a ReLU
# threshold moved to 0.01): every f32 row fails by 3-28×. The two deep bf16 rows are THIN —
# a swapped 3×3 kernel moved ResNet-34 bf16's median 0.16 → 0.43 and a swapped depthwise
# kernel moved MobileNetV2 bf16's 0.17 → 0.29, so their bounds sit 1.5-1.8× over the clean
# run. A sub-noise change (GELU's 0.044715 → 0.046 in one block) passes everywhere.
